speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing chronic left shoulder pain without any history of trauma. To begin my assessment, can you describe the specific location of the pain and whether it radiates to your neck, arm, or hand?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis). The clinical picture of chronic, insidious onset pain with significant limitation in both active and passive range of motion, particularly affecting daily activities, is classic for this condition. Given the patient's age and lack of trauma or neuropathic symptoms, this is the most likely diagnosis.
